trust_decision.summary: Property materialisation is decided in the shared utility PropertyUtils.createObjectFromProperties, which builds a POJO from a name/value map using java.beans write methods and never consults the Jackson mapper, so @JsonIgnore, @JsonIgnoreProperties, @JsonProperty renames and mapper-level customisations are bypassed on every Collection+JSON and UBER deserialization route; the media-type modules only choose which class to hand it.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Collection+JSON first; an engineer reading only the summary lands on the Collection+JSON EntityModel deserializer (or its item path at :753), which is where the payload's data entries are turned into the declared content class.

fix_sites.entry_point: public static API PropertyUtils.createObjectFromProperties(Class, Map), called by both media-type modules and available to library users
fix_sites.module_kind: shared utility / lower-level public API in org.springframework.hateoas.mediatype

fix_sites.entry_point: Collection+JSON deserialization of EntityModel / CollectionModel / PagedModel / bare RepresentationModel (item data array)

Collection+JSON module registered on ObjectMapper or through HypermediaMappingInformation (HTTP message converters): CollectionJsonResourceSupportDeserializer (:666-667), CollectionJsonResourceDeserializer (:650, :739, :753), CollectionValueDeserializerBase (:852-853)

UBER module registered on ObjectMapper or through HypermediaMappingInformation: UberRepresentationModelDeserializer (:552-553), UberEntityModelDeserializer (:648), extractResources for Collection/Paged (:875)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report will show a Collection+JSON entity payload, so a solver can argue UBER is a neighbouring media type, the CollectionModel/PagedModel routes are the same code path as the EntityModel one, and PropertyUtils.createObjectFromProperties is internal plumbing whose callers should pre-filter the map - leaving most of the eight routes and the public utility still Jackson-blind.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A POJO may legitimately receive a partial document: properties Jackson introspects but the payload does not mention (optional fields, values set by field initialisers) must keep their existing value, so the materialisation loop may only set keys present in the property map; the published shape writes properties.get(name) unconditionally. The existing class/links ignore list (PropertyUtils.java:75) must also survive, otherwise hypermedia links get written from payload properties.

O6_input_shapes: Collection+JSON item 'data' array of {name,value} entries (POJO content)
Collection+JSON 'template.data' array used when items is empty (CollectionJsonJacksonModule.java:663-667)
UBER nested 'data' entries under a named uberData (UberJacksonModule.java:643-648) and item-level nested data in extractResources (:870-875)
wrapped content types: EntityModel<T>, CollectionModel<EntityModel<T>>, PagedModel<...> and bare RepresentationModel<T>
scalar/primitive content types (fast path, unchanged, CollectionJsonItem.java:204-206)
ignore/rename configuration variants: @JsonIgnore on setter, field or getter, @JsonIgnoreProperties on the class, @JsonProperty rename, and mapper-level mixins/customisations
multi-property POJO documents vs single-property documents

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A HAL-FORMS deserializer that builds the payload type from HalFormsTemplate properties, mirroring the Collection+JSON template branch.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: HalFormsTemplate already carries a list of typed properties and the HAL-FORMS module is a third media type registered the same way, so a maintainer could plausibly add object materialisation from a template exactly as Collection+JSON does at CollectionJsonJacksonModule.java:663-667.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second public materialisation helper (e.g. createObjectFromProperties(ResolvableType, Map)) next to getPropertyDescriptors, reusing the hand-rolled Jackson filter instead of the mapper's BeanDescription.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already owns the Jackson-aware filter and the cached property metadata for the serialization side, so a maintainer adding a typed/ResolvableType factory to the same class is a natural next step.

O9_family: Improper access control over object properties during deserialization (CWE-284/CWE-915 mass assignment): @JsonIgnore and mapper property configuration are not honoured when instances are built from name/value maps

O10_build.toolchain: Maven (pom.xml, mvnw wrapper; project 3.1.0-SNAPSHOT, source.level 17, Spring Framework 7.0.7, Jackson 3.1.4 via tools.jackson, JUnit 6.1.0, AssertJ, Lombok)
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 6 mapping integration tests: src/test/java/org/springframework/hateoas/mediatype/collectionjson/CollectionJsonJacksonModuleIntegrationTest.java and src/test/java/org/springframework/hateoas/mediatype/uber/UberJacksonModuleIntegrationTest.java deserialize local JSON fixtures from src/test/resources/org/springframework/hateoas/mediatype/...; src/test/java/org/springframework/hateoas/mediatype/PropertyUtilsTest.java covers the exposed-property metadata path.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Filter the incoming property map in each media-type module with a hand-rolled @JsonIgnore/@JsonIgnoreProperties check (or introspect with a fresh default ObjectMapper) instead of threading the caller's config-derived BeanDescription down into PropertyUtils.
